text: The new document is version 3 and its internal Version row reads 3, taken from the highest version of the file family (v2) under Template and Rules R8.2, not from the internal Version row of version 2, which reads 1.
why: Version 2 gives Version 1 in its metadata while its file name is v2. Two versions of the same document cannot both describe the next issue.
read: Template and Rules v1 R8.2; 08 AI and agents/Recovery Workbench Model Integration Design v2.docx metadata table.
applied_in: Metadata table, Version row; title block line; section 6 change log.
impact: If the family numbering is not the document numbering, the issue is v2 and the internal row stays 2; no content changes.

text: The agent platform of DL33 is read as the rwb-agent service (P10, wave 1): its task queue rwb-agent, its AgentRunWorkflow and its activities are the only place a model endpoint call is made.
why: Version 2 names an agent platform and a tool gateway but no service. Architecture v5 gives P10 the agent runtime, the model endpoint call and the tool gateway.
read: Architecture v5 slide 16 and slide 41 (P10 rwb-agent: agent policies, prompts, runs, guardrails, evaluations); Ownership Map Services and Workflows and activities sheets; AI and Agent Architecture v2 slide 5.
applied_in: Sections 1 and 4, and the call table in section 4.
impact: If another service is the agent platform, the caller and the queue names in sections 1 and 4 change and the model-call rule moves with them.

text: The model version in force for each decision step, and the champion and challenger shares set by the same table, are reference data owned by rwb-case (P3) and reached through its reference-data contract (DP-07, RWB-P3-E1043-CON); the rule package registry stays with rwb-decision (P7).
why: Version 2 calls the version in force reference data and does not name a table or an owner. The R3 default ruling gives reference data to P3 rwb-case and the rule package registry to P7 rwb-decision, and the COLLINS model version is not a Drools rule package.
read: Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings and DP-07; Ownership Map Parameters sheet; Architecture v5 slide 41 P7 rule registry.
applied_in: Section 2 owner row and placeholder; section 3 owner table and paragraph.
impact: If the version in force belongs to rwb-decision with the rule registry, the P3 references in sections 2 and 3 become P7 and the reference-data dependency is dropped.

text: INT-08 is read as the ACE overnight ingestion of COLLINS into the ACE database, whose score output rwb-source-data (P1) reads through the v_ace_score view; the INT-08 reference is kept as version 2 writes it, and the owner of the interface in the target is left as the R9 placeholder.
why: Architecture v5 and Interface Specifications v3 do not name INT-08. The document must keep the ID as the source has it and must not invent an interface owner.
read: Architecture v5 slide 24 (ACE ingests COLLINS overnight; Recovery loads no source data) and the appendix interface list; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 v_ace_score over public.collins_score.
applied_in: Section 1 text after the model table; section 2 statement.
impact: If INT-08 is a live file interface with an owner, the placeholder is replaced and the P1 read is described as the load path instead of the interface.

text: The tool gateway of rwb-agent reaches two read-only targets: case facts and the score through the data-product contract of rwb-source-data (P1), and extracted document fields through the REST contract of rwb-document (P5); the gateway holds the permissions and the agent holds no credential.
why: Version 2 names the gateway but no target. Architecture v5 slide 16 names the two read-only tools and the Ownership Map gives the two contracts.
read: Architecture v5 slide 16; Ownership Map Endpoints and Tables sheets; AI and Agent Architecture v2 slide 8.
applied_in: Section 4 tool-gateway bullet and the call table in section 4.
impact: If the gateway reaches more systems, the call table gains rows; the model-endpoint rule is unchanged.

text: The three monitoring owner roles of version 2 are kept word for word, and the data each measure reads is attributed to its owner in the Ownership Map: score coverage to rwb-source-data (P1), drift to rwb-agent (P10) and rwb-decision (P7), outcome to rwb-source-data (P1) and rwb-decision (P7).
why: Version 2 names governance roles only. The Ownership Map gives an owner to every table, event and data product, and the roles are not changed by the realignment.
read: Ownership Map Tables, Events and Services sheets; Architecture v5 slide 41 (agent tables P10, decision ledger and approvals P7).
confirm: Model Risk and the data owners
impact: If a measure is read from another owner's data, the row changes owner; the roles and the review cycles stay.

text: D5.1 and D5.2 are kept exactly as version 2 writes them, with no service and no step owner assigned in this document.
why: Neither reference is defined in the source and no source in the read list names them, so any service assignment would be invented.

confirm: TechX and the treatment module owner

text: The document is issued with status Draft and no approval round in this run, as the D-RCV-60 overlay allows.
why: No human approval is required to proceed in this run; a missing approval status is recorded as an assumption and the document stays Draft.
impact: If an approval is required, the status changes and the approval is recorded; the content is unchanged.

text: The score, band and model version reach every service other than rwb-source-data (P1) through rwb-source-data's contract (the DP11 data product), never by reading the ACE views or another service's tables.
why: Architecture v5 and ADR-010 give the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views to rwb-source-data alone, and DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables; the model table's new column states this for every model row.
read: Architecture v5 slide 24 and the ADR-010 note; Template and Rules DP-01 and DP-05; Ownership Map Endpoints (GET /data-products/{productCode}/records, P1).
applied_in: Section 1 model table, Score read by column, and the text after it; section 2 owner row.
impact: If a service may read the views itself, the column changes for that service and DP-05 is amended instead.
